answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a pearl as the anchor of the cost. A bridge stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a orchard...
